sections.title: Meeting Time and Place
sections.content: Steve Crocker scheduled a Network Working Group meeting in room Astro VII of the Astroworld Hotel in Houston. It was set for 8:00 p.m. on Monday, 16 November 1970, during the Fall Joint Computer Conference.
sections.plainLanguage: The notice gives a time and place for a Network Working Group meeting in Houston. It is an announcement, not a report of what happened there.

sections.title: Topics for Practical Network Use
sections.content:
The proposed topics are accounting mechanisms, documentation distribution, person-to-person message sending and storage, and access to systems by foreign users. Attendees are invited to raise other topics.

Crocker expects smaller subsidiary meetings during the conference to pursue these or related subjects.
sections.plainLanguage: The group plans to discuss accounting, sharing documents, person-to-person messages and access for users from other sites. Participants may add topics, and smaller meetings may follow.

sections.title: Attendance and Follow-up
sections.content: Prospective attendees are asked to notify Benita Kirstel so organizers can make sure the room is large enough. The note says unexpected attendees are also welcome.
sections.plainLanguage: People planning to attend are asked to notify the organizer's secretary so the room can be prepared. The notice also welcomes people who arrive without advance notice.
